transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm here because... well, I just can't shake this absolute certainty that I'm being punished for letting my father decline. 

My sister tries to talk me out of it. She even shows me the doctor's notes and tells me I did everything right, but it doesn't matter. It just feels like... like some judgment has already been passed on me, and I can't get past it.
Have you noticed any changes in your senses, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others do not?

Yes, actually. Um... at night, when the house is really quiet, I sometimes hear a woman's voice. It sounds as clear as if she's standing right out in the hallway. She just says, "You failed him." I've actually gotten out of bed more than once to check who is speaking, even though... well, no one is ever there.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and hearing this voice?
It's been going on for about a year and two months now. That was... well, that's when my father's health and behavior really started changing, and I had to step in and take over his caregiving.
Have you found it difficult to keep your thoughts organized or have others mentioned that your speech is sometimes hard to follow?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My thoughts feel pretty clear to me, and no one at work or at home has said anything about my speech being hard to follow. I mean, I might get a little distracted sometimes because I'm so focused on... on everything that happened, but I can still hold a normal conversation.
Are there any other beliefs or ideas you hold that others seem to disagree with, or is this feeling specifically related to your father's passing?

It's really just focused on my father. I mean, the reason I came in is because I just can't shake this... this absolute certainty that I'm being punished for letting him decline. My sister tries to talk me out of it. She shows me the doctor's notes and tells me I did everything right, but... none of that changes how I feel. It just feels like some kind of judgment has already been passed on me, and there's no changing it.
Over the past year, have you experienced periods where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Yes. Honestly, most days I wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling. It's just there, like the color has gone out of everything. I can be sitting at my desk at work doing HR stuff, or even just looking out at my garden beds at home—things I used to care about—and it just feels like none of it really reaches me anymore. It's just a constant sadness.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this depressed, hopeless, or disconnected from life at any point in your past, prior to the events involving your father a year ago?

No, not really. I mean, I've had normal bad days or stressful weeks at work, like anyone else, but... never anything like this. Before my dad passed away, I was generally doing fine. I never felt this kind of constant sadness or hopelessness until all of that happened.
Have you ever had a similar period of feeling this depressed, hopeless, or disconnected from life at any time in your life prior to the events involving your father a year ago?

Like I just mentioned, no, I haven't. I've really never experienced anything like this before my dad passed away. My life was pretty normal before all of that happened. So, no, nothing like this in the past.
Since you've been feeling this way, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep?

Yes, my sleep has definitely been affected. I fall asleep pretty late now because I just lie in bed replaying old phone calls and all the care decisions I had to make. Then, when I finally do get to sleep, I'm wide awake again around 3 or 4 in the morning. My chest feels really tight, and I just... I can't get back to sleep before it's time to get up for work. As for my appetite, I haven't noticed a major change, but the sleep is a real problem.
